sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: In Mechanics Year 1, vertical projection used the suvat equations with acceleration \(g\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) downwards. Here objects can also be projected sideways.
\textbf{1: Horizontally projected}\par A particle is projected horizontally at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(50\,\mathrm m\) above the ground. How far along the ground does it travel?
\textbf{2: Projection at any angle}\par A cabbage is projected from ground level at \(30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at \(35^\circ\) to the horizontal. How far away does it hit the ground?

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: Consider vertical and horizontal motion separately.
Vertical acceleration downwards:
\(g\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Use the suvat equations.
Horizontal acceleration:
\(0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Velocity is constant, so \(\mathrm{speed}=\mathrm{distance}/\mathrm{time}\).

A particle is projected horizontally at \(25\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from \(78.4\,\mathrm m\) above a horizontal surface. Find:\par a. The time to reach the surface.\par b. The horizontal distance travelled.\par c. The distance of the impact point from the original point.
Take downwards as positive:\[s=78.4,\quad u=0,\quad a=9.8.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad78.4=4.9t^2.\]\[t=4\,\mathrm s.\]
Horizontally, use \(s=vt\):\[x=25\times4=100\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: A particle is projected horizontally at \(U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from \(122.5\,\mathrm m\) above a horizontal plane. It lands \(90\,\mathrm m\) horizontally from its starting point. Find its initial speed.

Take downwards as positive:\[s=122.5,\quad u=0,\quad a=9.8,\quad t\text{ unknown}.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[122.5=4.9t^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=5\,\mathrm s.\]Horizontally:\[90=U\times5\quad\Rightarrow\quad U=18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]

transcription.tex: A particle is projected horizontally at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from \(h\,\mathrm m\) above a horizontal plane. It lands \(100\,\mathrm m\) horizontally from its starting point. Determine \(h\).
Horizontally:\[t=\frac{100}{20}=5\,\mathrm s.\]Taking downwards as positive:\[s=h,\quad u=0,\quad a=9.8,\quad t=5.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[h=\tfrac12\times9.8\times5^2=122.5\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: 5. A particle moves horizontally at \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) along a flat smooth table, starting \(2\,\mathrm m\) from its edge. The table is \(1.2\,\mathrm m\) above the floor. Find the total time from projection until it lands on the floor.

On the table, horizontally:\[s=vt\quad\Rightarrow\quad2=20t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=0.1\,\mathrm s.\]After leaving the table, taking downwards as positive:\[u_y=0,\quad a=9.8,\quad s=1.2.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad1.2=4.9t^2.\]\[t^2=\frac{1.2}{4.9},\quad t=0.49487\ldots\,\mathrm s.\]Reject the negative root. Total time:\[0.1+0.49487\ldots=0.59\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 6. A dart is thrown horizontally at \(14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) towards a vertical dartboard. Model the dart as a particle moving freely under gravity, in a vertical plane perpendicular to the board. It hits \(9\,\mathrm{cm}\) below its launch level. Find the horizontal distance from the launch point to the board.

Take downwards as positive:\[u_y=0,\quad a=9.8,\quad s=0.09\,\mathrm m.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad0.09=4.9t^2.\]\[t^2=\frac{0.09}{4.9},\quad t=0.13552\ldots\,\mathrm s.\]Reject the negative root. Horizontally, \(u_x=14\):\[s=vt\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=14\times0.13552\ldots\]\[x=1.8973\ldots=1.90\,\mathrm m\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 7. A particle of mass \(2.5\,\mathrm{kg}\) is projected along a horizontal rough surface at \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). After \(2\,\mathrm m\), it leaves as a projectile and lands \(1.2\,\mathrm m\) below. Total time from projection to landing is \(1.0\,\mathrm s\). Find:\par a. The time in contact with the surface.\par b. The coefficient of friction between particle and surface.

After leaving the surface, take downwards as positive:\[u_y=0,\quad a=9.8,\quad s=1.2.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad1.2=4.9t^2.\]\[t=\sqrt{1.2/4.9}=0.49487\ldots\,\mathrm s.\]Time on surface:\[1-0.49487\ldots=0.50513\ldots\,\mathrm s.\]

On the surface, vertically \(R=mg\). Horizontally:\[F=ma\quad\Rightarrow\quad-\mu R=ma.\]\[-\mu mg=ma\quad\Rightarrow\quad a=-\mu g.\]With \(s=2\), \(u=5\), \(t=0.50513\ldots\):\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[2=5(0.50513\ldots)+\tfrac12a(0.50513\ldots)^2\]\[0.12757\ldots a=2-2.5256\ldots\]\[a=-4.1201\ldots\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]\[-4.1201\ldots=-9.8\mu\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mu=0.42042\ldots\]\[\mu=0.42\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: A particle \(P\) is projected from \(O\) on a horizontal plane at \(28\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at elevation \(30^\circ\). It moves freely under gravity until it strikes the plane at \(A\). Find:\par a. Its greatest height above the plane.\par b. Its time of flight.\par c. The distance \(OA\).
Take upwards as positive:\[u=28\sin30^\circ=14,\quad v=0,\quad a=-9.8.\]\[v^2=u^2+2as\quad\Rightarrow\quad0=14^2+2(-9.8)s.\]\[s=10\,\mathrm m.\]

Back at its original level, vertical displacement is \(0\):\[s=0,\quad u=14,\quad a=-9.8.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad0=14t-4.9t^2=t(14-4.9t).\]\[t=0\quad\text{or}\quad t=\frac{14}{4.9}=2.857\ldots\,\mathrm s.\]Time of flight is \(2.9\,\mathrm s\) (2 s.f.).
\[OA=28\cos30^\circ\times2.857\ldots\]\[=69.282\ldots=69\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: A particle is projected from \(O\) at \(V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at elevation \(\theta\), where \(\tan\theta=4/3\). Point \(O\) is \(42.5\,\mathrm m\) above a horizontal plane. The particle strikes the plane at \(A\) after \(5\,\mathrm s\).\par a. Show that \(V=20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par b. Find \(OA\).
Draw a diagram before solving.

\[\sin\theta=\frac45,\qquad\cos\theta=\frac35.\]Take upwards as positive:\[s=-42.5,\quad u=\frac45V,\quad a=-9.8,\quad t=5.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[-42.5=\frac45V\times5-4.9\times25\]\[V=20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]
Let the horizontal distance be \(x\):\[x=20\cos\theta\times5=\frac35(20)\times5=60\,\mathrm m.\]
By Pythagoras:\[OA=\sqrt{42.5^2+60^2}=73.527\ldots\]\[OA=74\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: A particle is projected from \(O\) at \(35\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at elevation \(30^\circ\). It moves freely under gravity. Find the length of time for which it is \(15\,\mathrm m\) or more above \(O\).\par Find the two times at height \(15\,\mathrm m\); subtract them.

Take upwards as positive:\[s=15,\quad u=35\sin30^\circ=17.5,\quad a=-9.8.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad15=17.5t-4.9t^2.\]\[4.9t^2-17.5t+15=0.\]Use the quadratic solver on your calculator:\[t=\frac{10}{7},\quad\frac{15}{7}.\]Time at or above \(15\,\mathrm m\):\[\frac{15}{7}-\frac{10}{7}=\frac57\approx0.71\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]The supplied textbook permits \(5/7\); the model uses approximate \(g=9.8\), so \(0.71\,\mathrm s\) expresses the physical precision.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Edexcel M2 (old), May 2012, Q7}\par A small stone is projected from \(O\), at the top of a vertical cliff \(OA\), \(52.5\,\mathrm m\) above the sea. It rises \(10\,\mathrm m\) above \(O\), then hits the sea at \(B\), with \(AB=50\,\mathrm m\). Model it as a particle moving freely under gravity.\par a. Show its initial vertical velocity component is \(14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). (3 marks)\par b. Find its speed of projection. (9 marks)\par c. Find the time when it moves parallel to \(OB\). (5 marks)
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]
At maximum height, \(v_y=0\):\[0=u_y^2-2(9.8)(10)\quad\Rightarrow\quad u_y=14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]

Upwards positive:\[-52.5=14t-\tfrac12gt^2\]\[49t^2-140t-525=0\]\[(t-5)(49t+105)=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=5\,\mathrm s.\]Horizontally, \(50=5u_H\), so \(u_H=10\).\[u=\sqrt{10^2+14^2}=\sqrt{296}=17.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]
\[\tan\angle OBA=\frac{52.5}{50}=1.05.\]When parallel to \(OB\), the downward vertical speed is \(1.05\times10=10.5\).\[-10.5=14-gt\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=2.5\,\mathrm s.\]

transcription.tex: 7. A particle is projected with initial velocity \(\mathbf U=3k\mathbf i+2k\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par a. Find the angle of projection.\par b. Given its initial speed is \(3\sqrt{13}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find \(k\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Let the angle of the velocity line be \(\alpha\):\[\tan\alpha=\frac{2k}{3k}=\frac23\]\[\alpha=33.690\ldots^\circ=33.7^\circ\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]This is above the positive horizontal for \(k>0\). If \(k<0\), the velocity points in the opposite direction.

Speed is the magnitude of velocity:\[(3\sqrt{13})^2=(3k)^2+(2k)^2\]\[9\times13=9k^2+4k^2\]\[117=13k^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad k^2=9\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\pm3.\]If projection is specified upwards and rightwards, only \(k=3\) applies.

transcription.tex: 9. A stone is thrown at \(30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) from a window \(20\,\mathrm m\) above horizontal ground. It hits the ground \(3.5\,\mathrm s\) later. Find:\par a. Its angle of projection.\par b. The horizontal distance from the window to its landing point.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Let \(\alpha\) be elevation above horizontal.\[u_x=30\cos\alpha,\qquad u_y=30\sin\alpha.\]Take upwards as positive:\[s=-20,\quad a=-9.8,\quad t=3.5.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[-20=30\sin\alpha\times3.5-4.9(3.5)^2\]\[\sin\alpha=\frac{4.9(3.5)^2-20}{30\times3.5}=0.381190\ldots\]\[\alpha=22.407\ldots^\circ\approx22^\circ\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]
Horizontally, \(u=30\cos22.407\ldots^\circ\), \(t=3.5\):\[s=ut=30\cos22.407\ldots^\circ\times3.5\]\[=97.072\ldots\approx97\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 10. A ball is thrown from \(O\) on horizontal ground at \(U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at elevation \(\theta\), where \(\tan\theta=3/4\). It strikes a vertical wall \(20\,\mathrm m\) from \(O\), \(3\,\mathrm m\) above the ground. Find:\par a. \(U\).\par b. The time from projection to striking the wall.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

\[\sin\theta=\frac35,\quad\cos\theta=\frac45,\quad u_x=\frac{4U}{5},\quad u_y=\frac{3U}{5}.\]Horizontally:\[20=\frac{4U}{5}t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{25}{U}.\]Vertically upwards:\[s=3,\quad a=-9.8,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2.\]\[3=\frac{3U}{5}t-4.9t^2.\]Substitute \(t=25/U\):\[3=\frac{3U}{5}\frac{25}{U}-4.9\frac{25^2}{U^2}=15-\frac{3062.5}{U^2}.\]\[U^2=\frac{3062.5}{12}=255.208\ldots\]\[U=15.975\ldots\approx16\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]
\[t=\frac{25}{U}=\frac{25}{15.975\ldots}=1.5649\ldots\]\[t=1.6\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: 11. Particle \(P\) is projected from \(A\), position \(20\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\) relative to fixed origin \(O\), with velocity \((5u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It moves freely under gravity through \(B\), position \((k\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), before reaching \(C\) on the \(x\)-axis. Travel from \(A\) to \(B\) takes \(4\,\mathrm s\). Find:\par a. \(u\).\par b. \(k\).\par c. The angle its velocity makes with the \(x\)-axis at \(C\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]
From \(A\) to \(B\), upwards positive:\[u_y=4u,\quad s=12-20=-8.\]\[a=-9.8,\quad t=4.\]\[s=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[-8=4u\times4-4.9\times4^2\]\[u=\frac{4.9\times4^2-8}{16}=4.4.\]
Horizontally from \(A\) to \(B\):\[u_x=5u=5(4.4)=22,\quad t=4.\]\[s=u_xt\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=22\times4=88.\]

\(v_x=22\) throughout. At \(C\):\[u_y=4(4.4),\quad a=-9.8,\quad s=-20.\]\[v_y^2=u_y^2+2as\]\[=(4\times4.4)^2+2(-9.8)(-20)\]\[=16(4.4)^2+392=701.76.\]The particle is descending:\[\tan\theta=\frac{|v_y|}{v_x}=\frac{\sqrt{701.76}}{22}.\]\[\theta=50.291\ldots^\circ\approx50^\circ\]below the positive \(x\)-axis (2 s.f.).

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: 12. A stone is thrown from \(A\) at \(30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(15^\circ\) below horizontal. Point \(A\) is \(14\,\mathrm m\) above horizontal ground. It strikes the ground at \(B\). Find:\par a. The time from \(A\) to \(B\).\par b. The distance \(AB\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Take downwards as positive:\[u_x=30\cos15^\circ,\quad u_y=30\sin15^\circ.\]\[s=14,\quad a=9.8.\]\[s=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[14=30t\sin15^\circ+4.9t^2\]\[4.9t^2+30t\sin15^\circ-14=0.\]The positive root is:\[t=\frac{-30\sin15^\circ+\sqrt{900\sin^215^\circ+4(14)(4.9)}}{9.8}\]\[=1.074\ldots\approx1.1\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

Horizontally, \(u_x=30\cos15^\circ\):\[s=u_xt=(30\cos15^\circ)(1.074\ldots)\]\[=31.136\ldots\,\mathrm m.\]\[AB^2=14^2+(31.136\ldots)^2=1165.456\ldots\]\[AB=34.138\ldots\approx34\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 13. A particle is projected from level ground at \(U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), at elevation \(\alpha\). Its maximum height is \(42\,\mathrm m\), and it lands \(196\,\mathrm m\) from projection. Find \(\alpha\) and \(U\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

\(u_x=U\cos\alpha\), \(u_y=U\sin\alpha\). At maximum height, \(v_y=0\), \(s=42\):\[v_y^2=u_y^2+2as\]\[0=U^2\sin^2\alpha-2g(42)\]\[U^2\sin^2\alpha=84g.\qquad(1)\]Find two expressions for flight time. Horizontally:\[196=U\cos\alpha\,t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{196}{U\cos\alpha}.\]Vertically back at ground level:\[0=Ut\sin\alpha-\tfrac12gt^2=t(U\sin\alpha-\tfrac12gt).\]Ignore \(t=0\):\[t=\frac{2U\sin\alpha}{g}.\]

Equate the times:\[\frac{196}{U\cos\alpha}=\frac{2U\sin\alpha}{g}\]\[U^2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha=98g.\qquad(2)\]Divide (1) by (2):\[\tan\alpha=\frac{84g}{98g}=\frac67\]\[\alpha=40.6^\circ\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]Substitute in (1), taking the positive speed:\[U\sin\alpha=\sqrt{84g}\]\[U=\frac{\sqrt{84(9.8)}}{\sin\alpha}\approx44\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: 15. An object is projected from fixed origin \(O\) at \((4\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It moves freely under gravity through \(P\), position \(k(\mathbf i-\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), where \(k>0\).\par a. Find \(k\).\par b.i. Find its speed at \(P\).\par b.ii. Find its direction of motion at \(P\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Horizontally, \(u_x=4\), \(s=k\):\[s=vt\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=4t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=k/4.\]Vertically at \(P\), upwards positive:\[u_y=5,\quad a=-9.8,\quad s=-k.\]\[s=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[-k=\frac{5k}{4}-4.9\frac{k^2}{16}.\]Divide by \(k>0\):\[\frac94=\frac{4.9k}{16}\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\frac{4\times9}{4.9}\]\[=7.3469\ldots\approx7.35\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

The particle is descending. For the angle below horizontal:\[\cos\alpha=\frac{v_x}{v}=\frac4{\sqrt{185}}.\]Alternatively use \(\tan\alpha=|v_y|/v_x\) or \(\sin\alpha=|v_y|/v\).\[\alpha=72.897\ldots^\circ\approx72.9^\circ\quad(3\text{ s.f.})\]below the horizontal.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: 16. A basketball player stands on the floor \(10\,\mathrm m\) from a basket at height \(3.05\,\mathrm m\). The ball is thrown from height \(2\,\mathrm m\), at \(40^\circ\) above horizontal. Model it as a particle moving in a vertical plane. It passes through the basket.\par a. Find its initial speed.\par b. State two factors ignored by modelling it as a particle.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Let initial speed be \(U\). Horizontally:\[u_x=U\cos40^\circ,\quad s=10,\quad10=Ut\cos40^\circ\]\[t=\frac{10}{U\cos40^\circ}.\]Vertically upwards, \(u_y=U\sin40^\circ\), \(a=-9.8\), \(s=3.05-2=1.05\):\[s=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[1.05=\frac{10U\sin40^\circ}{U\cos40^\circ}-4.9\left(\frac{10}{U\cos40^\circ}\right)^2\]\[1.05=10\tan40^\circ-\frac{490}{(U\cos40^\circ)^2}\]\[(U\cos40^\circ)^2=\frac{490}{10\tan40^\circ-1.05}\]\[U^2=\frac{490}{(10\tan40^\circ-1.05)\cos^240^\circ}\]\[U=10.665\ldots\approx10.7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]
The ball’s size and its rotation/spin are ignored.\par The projectile calculation also neglects air resistance. Weight is not ignored: it causes gravitational acceleration.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Extension}\par A ball is projected from level ground with fixed speed \(u_0\), at elevation \(\theta\). Prove its horizontal range is greatest at \(45^\circ\).\par Year 2 differentiation is required.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Take upwards as positive, \(s=0\), \(u=u_0\sin\theta\), \(a=-g\):\[0=u_0t\sin\theta-\tfrac12gt^2=t(u_0\sin\theta-\tfrac12gt).\]Ignoring \(t=0\), flight time is \(t=2u_0\sin\theta/g\). Horizontally:\[x=u_0\cos\theta\frac{2u_0\sin\theta}{g}=\frac{2u_0^2}{g}\sin\theta\cos\theta\]\[x=\frac{u_0^2}{g}\sin2\theta.\]Differentiate with \(\theta\) in radians:\[\frac{dx}{d\theta}=\frac{2u_0^2}{g}\cos2\theta=0\]\[2\theta=\frac\pi2\quad\Rightarrow\quad\theta=\frac\pi4=45^\circ.\]Here \(d^2x/d\theta^2=-4u_0^2/g<0\), so this is a maximum for \(0<\theta<90^\circ\).

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: You may be asked to prove general results using the same projectile methods.\par A particle is projected from a horizontal plane at speed \(U\), elevation \(\alpha\), and moves freely under gravity until it returns to the plane at \(B\). Find expressions for:\par a. The time of flight \(T\).\par b. The range \(R\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Take upwards as positive:\[s=0,\quad u=U\sin\alpha,\quad a=-g.\]\[s=ut+\tfrac12at^2\]\[0=(U\sin\alpha)t-\tfrac12gt^2=t(U\sin\alpha-\tfrac12gt).\]\[t=0\text{ at launch},\quad T=\frac{2U\sin\alpha}{g}.\]
Horizontally:\[R=U\cos\alpha\frac{2U\sin\alpha}{g}=\frac{2U^2}{g}\sin\alpha\cos\alpha.\]Use the double-angle formula for sine:\[R=\frac{U^2\sin2\alpha}{g}.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: A particle is projected at speed \(U\), elevation \(\alpha\), and moves freely under gravity. After horizontal displacement \(x\), its height above launch is \(y\).\par a. Show that\[y=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2}(1+\tan^2\alpha).\]A particle is projected from \(O\) on a horizontal plane at \(28\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It passes through \(B\), \(32\,\mathrm m\) horizontally from \(O\) and \(8\,\mathrm m\) above the plane.\par b. Find both possible elevations \(\alpha\), to the nearest degree.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]
Do not be intimidated by symbols: resolve horizontally and vertically as usual.

Horizontally:\[x=U\cos\alpha\,t.\qquad(1)\]Vertically:\[y=U\sin\alpha\,t-\tfrac12gt^2.\qquad(2)\]The target has no \(t\). Make \(t\) the subject in (1), then substitute in (2):\[t=\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}\]\[y=U\sin\alpha\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}-\frac g2\left(\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}\right)^2\]\[=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2}\sec^2\alpha\]\[=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2}(1+\tan^2\alpha).\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: A particle is projected at speed \(U\), elevation \(\alpha\), and moves freely under gravity. After horizontal displacement \(x\), its height above launch is \(y\).\par a. Show that\[y=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2}(1+\tan^2\alpha).\]A particle is projected from \(O\) on a horizontal plane at \(28\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It passes through \(B\), \(32\,\mathrm m\) horizontally from \(O\) and \(8\,\mathrm m\) above the plane.\par b. Find both possible elevations \(\alpha\), to the nearest degree.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

\[8=32\tan\alpha-6.4(1+\tan^2\alpha).\]This is quadratic in \(\tan\alpha\):\[6.4\tan^2\alpha-32\tan\alpha+14.4=0\]\[4\tan^2\alpha-20\tan\alpha+9=0\]\[(2\tan\alpha-1)(2\tan\alpha-9)=0\]\[\tan\alpha=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad\frac92\]\[\alpha=27^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad77^\circ.\]
For a fixed speed, there are generally two launch angles through a reachable point ahead. At the limiting reachable height, they coincide into one.

transcription.tex: Exam note: you may be asked to derive these results. Use the resolving and suvat techniques from this chapter rather than memorising formulae for solving problems.

For initial speed \(U\), elevation \(\alpha\), motion freely under gravity, returning to the same horizontal plane:\[\text{Time of flight}=\frac{2U\sin\alpha}{g}.\]\[\text{Time to greatest height}=\frac{U\sin\alpha}{g}.\]\[\text{Range}=\frac{U^2\sin2\alpha}{g}.\]\[\text{Trajectory: }y=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2}(1+\tan^2\alpha).\]Here \(y\) is height above launch and \(x\) is horizontal displacement.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

transcription.tex: 5. Use \(g=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) in this question. A particle is projected from \(O\) at speed \(U\), elevation \(\alpha\), and moves freely under gravity. Its horizontal displacement is \(x\), height above \(O\) is \(y\).\par a. Show that \(y=x\tan\alpha-gx^2/(2U^2\cos^2\alpha)\).\par A stone is thrown from \(P\) at the end of a pier, \(15\,\mathrm m\) above sea level, at \(8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and elevation \(40^\circ\). Model it as a particle moving freely under gravity.\par b. Find its horizontal distance from \(P\) when \(2\,\mathrm m\) above sea level.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

Horizontally, \(u_x=U\cos\alpha\):\[x=(U\cos\alpha)t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}.\]Vertically upwards, \(u_y=U\sin\alpha\), \(a=-g\):\[y=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[y=U\sin\alpha\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}-\frac g2\left(\frac{x}{U\cos\alpha}\right)^2\]\[y=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2}{2U^2\cos^2\alpha}.\]

\(U=8\), \(\alpha=40^\circ\), \(y=2-15=-13\), \(g=10\):\[-13=x\tan40^\circ-\frac{10x^2}{2(8^2)\cos^240^\circ}.\]\[0.13313\ldots x^2-0.83910\ldots x-13=0.\]Let \(a=10/(128\cos^240^\circ)\). The quadratic formula gives\[x=\frac{\tan40^\circ\pm\sqrt{\tan^240^\circ+52a}}{2a}.\]\[x=13.5234\ldots\quad\text{or}\quad-7.2206\ldots.\]Reject the negative root, which lies behind projection:\[x=13.5234\ldots\approx13.5\,\mathrm m\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 7. A volleyball player hits a ball towards a net \(9\,\mathrm m\) away, from height \(1.5\,\mathrm m\). It moves in a vertical plane perpendicular to the net and just passes over its top, \(2.4\,\mathrm m\) above ground. Model it as a particle projected from \(O\) at \(U\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), elevation \(\alpha\).\par a. Write expressions for horizontal and vertical displacements after \(t\) seconds and show at the net that\[0.9=9\tan\alpha-\frac{81g}{2U^2\cos^2\alpha}.\]\par b. Given \(\alpha=30^\circ\), find the speed as it passes over the net.
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]

After \(t\) seconds:\[x=U\cos\alpha\,t,\qquad y=U\sin\alpha\,t-\tfrac12gt^2.\]Horizontally:\[s=u_xt\quad\Rightarrow\quad9=U\cos\alpha\,t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac9{U\cos\alpha}.\]Vertically, \(u_y=U\sin\alpha\), \(a=-g\), \(s=2.4-1.5=0.9\):\[0.9=U\sin\alpha\frac9{U\cos\alpha}-\frac g2\left(\frac9{U\cos\alpha}\right)^2\]\[0.9=9\tan\alpha-\frac{81g}{2U^2\cos^2\alpha}.\]

\[\tan30^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt3},\quad\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\quad\sin30^\circ=\frac12.\]\[0.9=\frac9{\sqrt3}-\frac{4(81)g}{2U^2(3)}\]\[4.296\ldots=\frac{529.2}{U^2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad U=11.098\ldots.\]At the net, \(v_x=U\cos30^\circ=9.6117\ldots\).\[v_y^2=u_y^2+2as=(U/2)^2-2(9.8)(0.9)\]\[=13.15\ldots.\]\[v^2=v_x^2+v_y^2=105.53\ldots\]\[v=10.273\ldots\approx10.3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 8. Unit vectors \(\mathbf i\), \(\mathbf j\) point horizontally and vertically upwards. An object is projected from \(A\) on horizontal ground at \((k\mathbf i+2k\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(k>0\). It moves freely under gravity until it lands at \(B\) and immediately stops. Take \(A\) as origin, with position \((x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\).\par a. Show that \(y=2x-gx^2/(2k^2)\).\par b. Given range \(AB=R\) and maximum height \(H\), find in terms of \(k,g\): i. \(R\); ii. \(H\).
\textbf{Constant acceleration}\[v=u+at,\quad s=ut+\tfrac12at^2,\quad v^2=u^2+2as\]\[s=\tfrac{u+v}{2}t,\quad s=vt-\tfrac12at^2.\]
Horizontally, \(u_x=k\):\[x=kt\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=x/k.\]Vertically, \(u_y=2k\), \(a=-g\):\[y=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[y=\frac{2kx}{k}-\frac g2\left(\frac xk\right)^2\]\[y=2x-\frac{gx^2}{2k^2}.\]
At landing, \(x=R>0\), \(y=0\):\[0=2R-\frac{gR^2}{2k^2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\frac{gR^2}{2k^2}=2R.\]\[R^2=\frac{4Rk^2}{g}\quad\Rightarrow\quad R=\frac{4k^2}{g}.\]

At maximum height, symmetry gives\[x=\frac R2=\frac{2k^2}{g}.\]Substitute into the trajectory:\[H=2\frac{2k^2}{g}-\frac g{2k^2}\left(\frac{2k^2}{g}\right)^2\]\[H=\frac{4k^2}{g}-\frac{2k^2}{g}=\frac{2k^2}{g}.\]
